item.title: Agility Unveils Humanoid That Can Work Safely Alongside People
item.description: on Tuesday unveiled a new humanoid that is designed to safely work in close proximity to people, a milestone for an industry that typically separates robots from human workers. The latest humanoid from the Salem, Oregon-based company, the Digit 5, is designed to conduct complex work such as loading materials onto equipment, sorting parts, sequencing and inspecting items. That’s a step up from Agility’s previous humanoid, the Digit 4, which was known for its ability to stack plastic bins.

item.title: Glencore Faces $2 Billion Suit as It Alleges Radiant World Fraud
item.description: Glencore Plc accused Radiant World and associated companies of sending falsified invoices to lenders — just as a senior executive at the group of traders said they had filed a $2 billion lawsuit against Glencore. On Tuesday, Glencore said that it had ended all business with Radiant World and associated companies including Sapphire Minmetals, and “exited all obligations.” For the first time, it directly accused them of fraud, saying that it had “confirmed evidence” that Radiant World and associated companies had “sent falsified invoices and contracts as well as fabricated emails, which they fraudulently claimed to have received from Glencore personnel, to a number of financial institutions.” Bloomberg News reported in July that several major commodity traders had moved to cut ties with Radiant World amid concerns it had provided falsified documents to banks. Bloomberg News has reported previously that Glencore traded extensively with Radiant World, helping it secure financing and even acquiring warrants that gave it the option to take a minority stake in the smaller company.

item.title: When 30 Seconds Isn’t Enough: Responding to Hesitation and Refusal
item.description: View Series In our previous article, “30 Seconds or Less: Building Trust at the Front Door” we covered the importance of the first few moments of an unexpected visit: identify yourself, explain the reason for the visit, bring the subject’s guard down, and give them a reason to trust you. But what happens when you do all that successfully – and the answer is still no? Hesitation : “I don’t know if I should sign this.” Many people are afraid of signing something they may not understand.

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Creates New Risks, Opportunities for Insurers
item.description: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is creating a wave of data center construction and, along with it, unprecedented risks and opportunities for insurers. “This has certainly taken over the market from a conversation perspective, and it’s something that we’re working on day in and day out,” said Jon Tellekamp, chief underwriting officer for Construction and Energy at AXA XL, in a recent interview for Carrier Management’s quarterly web series, Between the Lines.

item.title: Crypto firms get guidance on how the new regime applies
item.description: New FCA guidance will help firms understand how the law underpinning the UK's future cryptoasset regime applies to their business. David Geale, executive director of consumers, payments and competition at the FCA, said: 'We are building a crypto regime that firms, consumers and international partners can trust. This guidance gives firms the clarity they’ve asked for so they can prepare with confidence.' This guidance follows the FCA's extensive work to prepare for the new regime, including finalising its rules and guidance in June 2026 .

item.title: ILS offers diversification when traditional stock/bond relationships falter: Omnigence Asset Management
item.description: Given insurance-linked securities’ (ILS) ability to offer a bounded allocation whose premium compensates for real and imperfectly correlated tail risk, a new paper by Omnigence Asset Management suggests that ILS remains one of the most credible candidates for diversification when traditional stock-bond relationships falter. Given this, Omnigence Asset Management states that a record this short, across a period that has not included a sustained clustering of severe insured-loss years, may understate the overall frequency and depth of drawdowns that a full loss cycle could produce. In the firm’s recently published report, executives outlined that the diversifying leg of the traditional portfolio depends on stocks and bonds moving in opposite directions, an assumption that has broken down in periods when inflation is elevated and correlations turn positive.

item.title: EU Touts Climate Insurance Pact to Ease Catastrophe Losses
item.description: The European Union will set up a “climate insurance alliance” to help pay for losses as global warming increases the frequency and intensity of droughts, floods and wildfires. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the initiative as part of her state of the union address Wednesday, saying that only a quarter of catastrophe losses are privately insured, and that the costs therefore fall on national budgets. A climate resilience framework, due next month, will map 100 of the most vulnerable regions in the bloc, she added.

item.title: Ukraine Considers Ship Insurance to Revive Food Exports, Farm Groups Say
item.description: Ukraine is examining whether additional insurance cover for ships carrying food exports could help revive seaborne trade disrupted by Russian attacks on vessels and port infrastructure, a farm lobby group and a major farmers’ union said on Wednesday. The introduction of ship-insurance mechanisms was discussed,” the UCAB lobby group said in a report issued after a meeting with Ukraine’s president and prime minister. Since the summer, Russia has sharply stepped up attacks on Ukrainian seaports and commercial vessels, effectively halting the country’s seaborne exports.

item.title: Amazon’s AWS Facilities in Bahrain, UAE Still Not Restored From Iran War Damage
item.description: Amazon Web Services cannot restore access to its cloud-computing facility in Bahrain and one of three data – hosting zones in the United Arab Emirates following damage during the Iran war, according to a status update seen by Reuters on Tuesday. Amazon’s cloud computing unit AWS said the damage in Bahrain spanned multiple so-called availability zones, which are clusters of one or more data centers in the same geographic region. Read more: Drone Strikes Damage Amazon Data Centers in the UAE and Bahrain In the UAE, AWS said it was unable to restore access to resources and data hosted exclusively in one availability zone, known as mec1-az2.

item.title: Verisk and Qantev collaborate to help health insurers in APAC and GCC markets
item.description: Verisk and Qantev, an AI claims intelligence platform for health and life insurers, have announced a collaboration for insurers in the Asia-Pacific and Gulf Cooperation Council markets, designed to help health and life insurers make more precise underwriting decisions while improving claims efficiency. The collaboration brings together Verisk’s Health Risk Rating Tool, which helps insurers assess declared pre-existing medical conditions and generate data-driven risk scores, with Qantev’s AI-powered claims platform. We are excited to help the market transition away from rigid exclusions and toward smart, data-backed protection.” Iain Howie, managing director of life, health, and travel at Verisk, said insurers were seeking practical ways to expand access to cover.

item.title: NFP acquires Moores Insurance Management
item.description: NFP has acquired Moores Insurance Management, a multi-disciplinary risk management firm based in Minneapolis, Minnesota. “Moores is a long-standing risk management firm and this addition further establishes our presence in the Minnesota market and positions us well to continue delivering P&C insurance solutions for high-net-worth and commercial clients,” said Woodward. Mark Moores, the firm’s chief executive officer, joins NFP as senior vice president of commercial P&C, reporting to Amanda Ruback, managing director of P&C for NFP’s Central region.

item.title: Patra Launches Agentic Managed Services
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Patra (El Dorado Hills, Calif.) has launched managed services designed to orchestrate entire insurance operations workflows using agentic AI. Agentic AI With Expert Review Patra says its managed services are powered by an agentic AI platform built from years of investment and workflow knowledge developed through managing insurance processes at scale. Patra says its managed services use AI to execute related operational tasks in sequence, with quality checks in the platform and review by insurance professionals at key points.

item.title: Monitaur Offers FlightSim Standalone
item.description: (Image source: Monitaur FlightSim webpage.) Monitaur (Boston) has made FlightSim, the objective validation capability inside its AI governance platform, available as a standalone solution. “As the proliferation and impacts of AI and agents continue to accelerate, human review capacity and generalized evaluation, testing, and validation techniques fall short.” Clark says making FlightSim available as a standalone offering will let a broader group of companies use Monitaur’s AI validation expertise without adopting the full governance platform. Monitaur says standalone availability will let companies use FlightSim in deployment stacks and vendor-management security processes.

item.title: Capital markets, ILS well-structured to absorb data centre nat cat risks: Howden
item.description: The challenge is that values are now concentrated at single locations and clustered within a handful of high-hazard regions, creating exposures beyond what the traditional market can absorb efficiently alone.” Turning attention to the capital markets, Howden said: “This is precisely the type of risk the capital markets are structured to take on, with catastrophe peak risk being the original asset class for insurance-linked securities (ILS). Howden sees this as a prime opportunity for the capital markets, as catastrophe peak risk remains the foundations of the insurance-linked securities (ILS) asset class. According to Howden’s new report, in the US, a significant number of major data centre hubs are located in areas highly exposed to extreme weather, while on a global scale, more digital infrastructure is being developed in areas affected by armed conflict.

item.title: Texas Utility Discloses Customer Data Breach in SEC Filing
item.description: The Texas-based utility said it activated its cybersecurity incident response protocols and enlisted third-party cybersecurity experts after learning of the post, while also taking steps to further protect its systems. CenterPoint Energy CNP.N said in an SEC filing on Monday that the company had become aware in September of an online post by a third party claiming to have obtained a dataset of information on some of its customers. It has incurred and expects to continue incurring expenses tied to the incident and its response, the utility said, adding that it carries cybersecurity insurance it believes will offset related costs.

item.title: Iowa DIFS Names Pearce Acting Deputy Commissioner for Market Regulation
item.description: The Iowa Department of Insurance and Financial Services announced the appointment of Julie Pearce as Acting Deputy Insurance Commissioner for Market Regulation. With Pearce assuming this position, Jared Kirby will transition to the role of Senior Advisor to the Commissioner. Pearce brings over 19 years of extensive insurance and financial services experience spanning Life, Annuity, and Property & Casualty lines to the role.

item.title: California Governor Signs Act to Create Smoke Damage Presumption
item.description: The bill, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson and sponsored by California Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara, creates a presumption that smoke damage within a wildfire impact area resulted from the wildfire. AB 1795 directs the California Department of Insurance and CalOES to evaluate challenges posed by smoke damage and develop recommendations to strengthen protections for property insurance consumers and communities affected by future contamination events. Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1795, the Smoke Damage Recovery Act.

item.title: $40m Series A: AIUC raises funding to build insurance and certification infrastructure for AI agents
item.description: The post $40m Series A: AIUC raises funding to build insurance and certification infrastructure for AI agents appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Founded in 2025, AIUC is building the insurance, audit, and certification infrastructure needed to bring AI agents into the enterprise world. The capital will help extend AIUC’s audits, standards, and insurance from agents to frontier models.

item.title: Cedar Trace plans $300 million Lloyd’s syndicate
item.description: Cedar Trace Underwriting plans to launch a $300 million Lloyd’s syndicate for the 2027 underwriting year after receiving in-principle approval from the Lloyd’s Council. Capital is expected to come primarily from existing shareholders of Mereo Insurance and investors in Cedar Trace Capital Management’s insurance-linked securities funds. Cedar Trace was established in 2024 and is led by insurance veteran Brian Duperreault.

item.title: OpenAI Says It’s Working With Anthropic, Google on AI Safety
item.description: OpenAI is working on steps to address artificial intelligence safety issues with its top competitors Anthropic PBC and Google DeepMind, escalating industry efforts to respond to a groundswell of concern that the technology poses an economic and security threat. Chris Lehane, the global policy chief for OpenAI, said Tuesday that the company’s engagement with Anthropic and Google had been under way for several weeks. He added that OpenAI does not see the need for an antitrust waiver for the three AI firms to coordinate on safety matters.

item.title: Renoir Paintings Worth a Fortune Until Stolen
item.description: Two Renoir paintings stolen from a small French museum have yet to be recovered but if the thieves are hoping to cash in on the artwork, they would be hard-pressed to find a buyer. And unlike other eye-catching artifacts such as jewels, paintings can’t be chopped up and sold for parts without losing their entire worth. Sometimes that means paintings valued at millions of dollars are effectively “worth zero” once they’re outside of the museum, he added, if not a small fraction of the price.

item.title: New Vehicle Ownership Costs Hit $12,863 Annually: AAA
item.description: Despite EVs and hybrids joining mainstream vehicle comparisons, fuel savings don’t offset higher ownership costs. Vehicle type and purchase price both have a significant effect on depreciation for EV shoppers; for example, EV medium sedans had about twice the depreciation of gas-powered models, helping push total ownership costs 29.1% higher in that category. By comparing select electric and hybrid models within the same categories as gas-powered vehicles, shoppers get a more practical view of how ownership costs compare across powertrains, AAA explained.

item.title: Financial regulator bans former law firm owner from financial services
item.description: The FCA has banned Nurul Miah, also known as Neil Mia and Neil Miah, from working in financial services. The FCA has concluded that Mr Miah’s actions showed he lacked the honesty and integrity needed to work in financial services. Mr Miah was approved by the FCA in 2016 to work in senior management roles at an unconnected firm, Oracle Consultants Ltd.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: AI Takes A Growing Share Of Sales And Marketing Startup Funding
item.description: Unsurprisingly, AI-focused companies are capturing a much larger share of funding than during the prior peak, with most sales, marketing and CRM investment going to companies in Crunchbase AI-related categories. The numbers: So far in 2026, startups in sales, marketing and CRM have raised $7.5 billion globally across 830 funding rounds, Crunchbase data shows. Startups across sales, marketing and customer management have raised $7.5 billion so far this year, according to Crunchbase data.

item.title: AI Is Creating Wealth Faster Than Financial Lives Can Adapt
item.description: The gap between life experience and the sudden reality of managing serious wealth is widening as AI-native companies reach major valuations faster and private company liquidity arrives earlier. A June 2026 AWS study of more than 3,400 founders and senior leaders across 20 countries found that AI-native startups are reaching billion-dollar valuations in about 3.5 years, roughly half the time it took before generative AI. We recently advised founders who went from launching their company to a major liquidity event in less than a year.

item.title: KCC updates RiskInsight cat modeling platform to drive automation and data efficiency
item.description: Karen Clark & Company (KCC), the catastrophe risk modelling specialist, has launched RiskInsight® 4.16, the latest version of its RiskInsight open loss modeling platform, which introduces advanced performance, automation, and scalability enhancements for insurers, reinsurers, and insurance-linked securities (ILS) managers. The platform’s extensive API capabilities help (re)insurers automate critical modeling workflows, integrate RiskInsight more deeply into their existing systems, and manage large portfolios with greater efficiency.” RiskInsight’s extensive API suite supports integration with modeling, underwriting, and portfolio management systems, which enables re/insurers and ILS managers to integrate the KCC models into existing workflows.

item.title: MembersCap launches cat bond fund, was sole investor behind innovative cat / cyber ILW
item.description: Members Capital Management Limited (MembersCap) executives told us the company has recently launched its first catastrophe bond fund strategy to expand its offering to clients, while also disclosing that it was the investor behind a recent innovative industry-loss warranty (ILW) transaction. Dr Ben Fox, Co‑Founder & Chief Investment Officer of MembersCap told Artemis, “This summer we launched a new catastrophe bond strategy — a liquid, actively‑managed portfolio of 144A cat bonds that sits alongside our private reinsurance fund. MembersCap then completed the investment of its initial reinsurance portfolio through its MCM Fund I back in July 2025 , with that strategy becoming the first tokenised, institutional-grade reinsurance investment fund, designed to open new capital channels to both digital asset investors and traditional allocators.

item.title: Aon Raises $13.5 Billion From Bond Sale to Fund USI Takeover
item.description: Aon Plc raised $13.5 billion from a high-grade bond offering to help fund its planned acquisition of USI Insurance Services, marking one of the biggest M&A financing deals to come to market in 2026. Investors placed as much as $65 billion of orders on the sale, with the longest maturity drawing the most demand, according to people familiar with the matter. The $13.5 billion note offering marked the year’s second-largest high-grade bond deal tied to mergers and acquisitions, trailing only Abbott Laboratories’ $20 billion transaction in February.

item.title: Magnum Says Ben & Jerry’s Chair Fostered Toxic Culture
item.description: Ben & Jerry’s former independent chair Anuradha Mittal was “abusive, discriminatory and unprofessional” and fostered a toxic culture before she stepped down from the board earlier this year, according to a legal filing by Magnum Ice Cream Company. Read More: Ben & Jerry’s Co-Founder Says Brand Being ‘Destroyed’ by Magnum In August, a federal judge dismissed large parts of the independent board members’ complaint, including claims that Magnum tried to censor Ben & Jerry’s stance on progressive issues and silence Mittal. These counterclaims accompany Magnum’s legal defense against allegations that it wrongfully removed Ben & Jerry’s independent board directors from their roles, and failed to honor an agreement resolving the dispute over the sale of Ben & Jerry’s intellectual property rights in Israel.

item.title: Ryan Specialty Unit Withdraws Protest Over FL Commercial Clearinghouse Contract
item.description: Ten days after giving notice that it planned to protest the awarding of a contract to manage a clearinghouse for Florida’s Citizens Property Insurance commercial policies, Ryan Services Group has withdrawn the notice. The commercial clearinghouse contract with Bridge Specialty has not been finalized, and an estimate on what it’s worth was not available Tuesday morning. “Although we are disappointed that Risk Market Infrastructure, a Ryan Specialty subsidiary, was not selected as the administrator, we remain very supportive of the concept of a clearinghouse and will be pulling for its success.” The statement added: “We are as committed as we always have been to the Florida market and will continue to invest in bringing innovative specialty lines insurance solutions to our clients in Florida and everywhere else.” Citizens announced Sept.

item.title: AXA targets AI-led growth under new “Growing Forward” strategic plan
item.description: AXA has unveiled “Growing Forward”, its strategic plan for 2027 through 2029, focused on organic growth, artificial intelligence, and prevention. “With ‘Growing Forward,’ we are building the AXA of tomorrow: a high-performing and competitive AXA, an innovative AXA that listens to its customers’ needs, an AXA that contributes to a more resilient and inclusive society. AXA is targeting annual underlying earnings-per-share growth of 7% to 9% between 2026 and 2029, along with an underlying return on equity of 15% to 17%.

item.title: Allianz UK expands digital financial lines offering
item.description: Allianz UK has expanded the range of financial lines risks brokers can place digitally through QuoteSME, its proprietary broker trading platform, and imarket, a UK commercial insurance distribution network operated by Polaris. Allianz has also improved its company data enrichment for D&O customers, increasing match rates from 60% to 96%. Complete Directors & Officers is now available for businesses with turnover of up to £200 million, while Complete Professional Indemnity can accommodate businesses with fee income of up to £10 million and turnover of up to £100 million.

item.title: Andy Scurto to Lead OneShield Product Advisory Committee
item.description: Marlborough, MA — September 10, 2026 – OneShield today announced that Andy Scurto has been named Head of its Product Advisory Committee (PAC). As Head of the PAC, Scurto will sit at the intersection of OneShield’s product organization and the market it serves. item.title: Samsara launches driver rewards program
item.description: Connected operations platform Samsara has launched Driver Perks, a free rewards program for professional drivers in its network. Eligible drivers can access the program through the Samsara Driver App, a web link or a QR code provided by their employer. Samsara developed the program with input from its Driver Council and surveys of drivers across its network.

item.title: Rodrigo Vázquez, nuevo director general de onRisk
item.description: Grupo Mutua Propietarios ha nombrado a Rodrigo Vázquez director general de onRisk, su agencia de suscripción especializada en riesgos especiales. El directivo asumirá la responsabilidad de impulsar el crecimiento y consolidación de la agencia, tanto a través de su cartera actual como mediante el desarrollo de nuevas líneas de negocio y productos.

item.description: Howden Iberia anunciará hoy la incorporación de dos nuevos profesionales a su equipo de Construcción e Infraestructuras. Se trata, según adelantamos, de Alba Ventura Castro, como ejecutiva de cuentas sénior, y Alfredo Requena Deu, como asesor de construcción e infraestructuras.

item.description: China’s industry ministry unveiled a roadmap last week to strengthen its smart electric vehicle industry, targeting large-scale deployment of autonomous-driving vehicles by 2030 and greater global influence for its auto sector. item.title: Chemours, DuPont, Corteva Settle North Carolina ‘Forever Chemicals’ Claims for $455M
item.description: Chemours, DuPont and Corteva last week reached a $455 million settlement with North Carolina and 11 local entities over PFAS contamination claims tied to Chemours’ Fayetteville Works plant and other historical discharges. In line with a 2021 agreement among the companies, Chemours will bear 50% of the settlement cost, while DuPont and Corteva will split the remainder. It also covers North Carolina’s claims over PFAS contamination unrelated to Fayetteville Works, including pollution linked to aqueous film-forming foam.

item.title: The Adjuster Tenure Problem
item.description: View Series Insurance has a talent problem. A claims team can absorb losing one experienced adjuster, but what happens when it loses ten? Annual attrition among adjusters runs close to 20% industry-wide , and it’s markedly higher among lower-tenure, early-career adjusters than among the veterans they’re meant to eventually replace.
